key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but accelerates thermal-aging losses that spread into the absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive measurements can help engineers distinguish initial interface-passivation benefits from long-term thermal-stability trade-offs.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe depth-dependent photoluminescence.
Track recombination changes in PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret PL decays using diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced fullerene-deposition-induced interfacial losses after treatment, followed by faster degradation during thermal aging; simulations support surface- and bulk-recombination interpretations.
watch_item: Depth assignments are model-supported interpretations, and the abstract provides no quantitative degradation rates or device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
